title: [observability] After a restart the Bridge reads a long-idle transcript through: a full read leaves the execution due, so a message to a long-idle session reads as taken and its turn is logged (LOOK 4082)
prompt:
Spawn, objective 241 [observability] (the lead's contract of 2026-11-19 21:4x, from rev-e's LOOK 4082, sync/look-4082-rev-e.md; author rev-e; readers rev-f, then rev-b): after a restart, the Bridge reads a long-idle engine's transcript through to its new lines, so a message typed into it reads as taken and its turn is logged.

Base: live main 337c94b5.

The problem (alert message_not_taken:4082 to agent_supervisor, 2026-11-19 20:22):
- After a restart the Bridge rebuilds each running execution's transcript follow from the log. Its offset is execution.started's transcript_from: where the execution began, not how far its transcript was read. For exec_2851 that is 15.8 MB, from 11-16.
- With a watch set, follow_output reads only when the watch says the file changed (or the execution is due), at most READ_LIMIT (8 MiB) per read, and each read clears the change.
- So after a restart the Bridge works through the old lines at one 8 MiB read per change of the file. Those lines' events are in the log already (source_event_id), so nothing new comes of them.
- The supervisor was idle from 08:52 and 335 MB behind after the 20:10 restart. Its one turn at 20:20 changed the file a few times; the Bridge never reached the turn's lines.
- The message read as not taken, and the turn, its usage and its tools were missing from the log. Every deploy restart sends it back to the start.

Read first: crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs (Follow, follow_output, read_followed, due_to_read, the World tests and World::restart); crates/spawn-core/src/port.rs (READ_LIMIT); rsi/scenarios/214.sh (the world 241.sh builds on).

What changes (crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs only):
(1) A read that came back full (bytes.len() >= its limit) leaves the execution due (follow.due_at = now; one line, so follow_output stays within clippy's 100 lines): the next pass reads again, without waiting for a change of the file. A backlog of N bytes is read in about N / 8 MiB passes (the loop's pass is 500 ms), not in N / 8 MiB changes of the file.
(2) Nothing else moves. A read that is not full clears the change as before. The offset rule (a shrunk or replaced file is read again from the start), the half-written-line rule, the over-long-line skip and the one-checkpoint-per-read rule are as they were.
Not done: restoring the offset from how far the transcript was read. It would need a new record of the read offset; (1) alone makes the restart's re-read finish in passes, and the timing below shows that is fast enough at live size.

Files: crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs (the rule, two tests); owner: rsi/scenarios/241.sh (new), rsi/backlog/241.json.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/241.sh, black box, 214's world: a real spawn loop (the Bridge, the dispatcher, the alerts step) runs one ephemeral worker on 045's fake engine in take mode. Once the worker has taken its task and is idle:
- BB241_BULK_MIB (64) MiB of lines that carry no event are appended to its transcript in one write;
- the loop is restarted, and the engine stays idle 10 s;
- then a person's input. SPAWN_MESSAGE_TAKEN_SECS=12, SPAWN_ALERT_CHECK_SECS=1.
Checked:
- (1) the input is taken within 40 s of being typed, and 20 s after its bound no message_not_taken alert was ever fired for it;
- (2) its turn is logged: a turn.stopped of the session, read from its transcript, since the input was typed;
- (3) the task's lines read before the restart are not logged twice: the session's turn.stopped and message.taken counts from before the input equal those from before the restart.
On live main 337c94b5 (and 9e1a8d22), 241.sh exits 1 at (1).

Tests (unit, bridge.rs):
- a_backlog_over_one_read_is_read_through_without_another_change: 20 MiB of lines, then a tool line, in one write: read within 4 passes with no further change, and nothing read twice;
- after_a_restart_a_long_transcript_is_read_through_to_its_new_lines: the same transcript, a restart, one more line: its event is logged, the old one not twice.
No test is renamed or dropped.

Polled-read cost (the lead's condition): a restart re-reads every running engine's transcript from its execution's start, now in passes. The proof times it at live size (runs/t241.sh, a 313 MB transcript at twice the supervisor's event density with a turn end every ~190 KB): the first reading, and the restart's reading again, where every event is in the log already. GET /api/fleet/<session>/commands and GET /api/alerts are timed every 0.5 s throughout, against an idle baseline. Measured (runs/): the first reading of 313 MB (15,702 new events) 47.6-65.3 s; the restart's reading again, to a line written right after the restart, 13.4-15.6 s; the serve's two reads at p95 17-42 ms during either, as idle (p95 23-63 ms, the higher on a host at load 10); no loop warning.

Verified by: after landing and a loop restart, on live, the next message to agent_supervisor reads as taken (no message_not_taken alert), and its turn's events (message.taken, turn.stopped) are in the log (the lead's look, with GET /api/alerts).
